notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 with run_id retriage-drivers-1-053, reviewed_by stays null; no human reviewed or tested anything, no hardware was attached, and no MuJoCo engine, GPU, Isaac Lab, FlashCHORD, Newton/Warp/JAX or robot run is claimed.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD/RECON: the card names flash_chord.envs.rl:RLEnv as its entry symbol. The class exists at robotic_grounding/flash_chord/src/flash_chord/envs/rl.py:198, but it is a GPU/JAX/Warp training environment built at run time from a parquet reference and an embodiment configuration (scene/setup.py:29-86); it has no fixed MJCF file and no mujoco module call, so MujocoDriver cannot express it and the fake gate cannot construct it without a GPU, Newton, Warp and JAX. The card's models list names MuJoCo XML files; scene_29dof.xml is the only scene and the G1 whole-body planner loads it for forward kinematics (planner/g1_planner.py:104-110, 406-411). The package therefore serves that MuJoCo world through MujocoDriver, reading the model in place from the read-only clone. No Python native exists and native.py is not used. RLEnv, the Isaac Lab Sharpa-V2D tasks and the FlashCHORD/Newton/Warp/JAX training and replay stack are NOT COVERED; they would need their own integration when the SDK can carry that interface.

WHAT IT SERVES: cap.world.step.v1 {ticks, action:{ctrl:[29 numbers]}} and cap.world.reset.v1. The scene includes g1_29dof.xml (scene_29dof.xml:1-2), which has one free joint floating_base_joint on the pelvis at pos 0 0 0.793 and 29 hinge joints (g1_29dof.xml:63-67, 386-419), giving 36 qpos, 35 qvel and 29 ctrl entries. The actuator block declares 29 motor ctrlranges (hips +/-88, knees +/-139, ankles +/-50, waist yaw +/-88 and roll/pitch +/-50, arms +/-25, wrist pitch/yaw +/-5; g1_29dof.xml:387-419); the MuJoCo bridge derives those per-element bounds and the driver declares none of its own. cap.world.seed.v1 is not served by MujocoBridge; the reset class's seed field is accepted but mj_resetData does not use a seed. The world state is {time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed, native_checkpoint}.

SAFETY: risk R0 reflects isolated in-process simulated state (MHS-004 SAFE-006); no physical actuator, robot or hardware command is exposed. The runtime's software e-stop latch blocks step and reset until mhs.safety.reset, while the state stays readable; it is not a hardware emergency stop and makes no physical-safety claim. No estop_physical_ref is claimed. The model's ctrlranges are simulation values, not a physical torque certification.

FAKE: the fake backend is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco module, not the upstream simulator. It parses the same scene and its include for joint shape, qpos0, timestep and actuator ctrlranges and advances a placeholder joint state: each motor's force accelerates only its own hinge against a placeholder unit inertia and damping; it loads no mesh/texture/inertia/contact, resolves no friction/tendon/equality/force constraint and uses the bridge's basic snapshot profile (time, qpos, qvel, act, ctrl; no mj_getState/mj_setState, no warm-start). The model states no <option timestep>; the fake's 2 ms tick is a placeholder matching MuJoCo's library default, not a model value, and is disclosed in the fidelity gaps and the placeholder comments. The real sim path would be the official mujoco engine loading the same scene; it was not installed or run, the scene was never compiled and no trajectory was compared with the engine. Fidelity is F0 for the fake and F1 described for the real engine path.

WARNINGS: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND are the SDK's simulator-family warnings for a class-object backend (the fake is the family's mujoco stand-in, so native calls are not recorded and there is no upstream class surface to check); G8.NO_UNIT x3 is expected for the bridge-derived ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed inputs. PLAYBOOK.md section 8 lists these as expected for Gymnasium/MuJoCo drivers. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings: every Fact cites a line that exists at the pinned commit and no bound is declared in the driver.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds seven cases: model shape from the scene (36 qpos, 35 qvel, 29 ctrl, qpos0, ctrlranges), step applying ctrl and advancing ticks/time, reset restoring model defaults, malformed inputs rejected before state change, out-of-envelope ctrl refused before state change, e-stop latching step with readable state and reset releasing it, and repeatability of the placeholder state hash. All pass, as does G9.

LICENCE: the card pins CC-BY-4.0 AND Apache-2.0; robotic_grounding setup.py:36 declares Apache 2.0, while the MuJoCo model assets carry a Unitree BSD 3-Clause licence (planner/assets/mujoco/NOTICE:3-6, LICENSE:1-3). The owner decides before publication (publish_review not_required for this card, but the asset licence is recorded).

NOT COVERED: flash_chord.envs.rl:RLEnv, the Isaac Lab Sharpa-V2D tasks, the FlashCHORD/Newton/Warp/JAX training and replay stack, the scene's sensor readings, and any physical G1. The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed); no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Reviewed the pinned MJCF, all 18 facts, the model stop/reset semantics and the excluded FlashCHORD interface; the fake gate and strict collector pass. Corrected the planner-load citation and the unsupported GPU-only explanation, added literal Scene/Reference, Warp-return and CPU/CUDA facts, and disclosed retained controls and the absence of an external simulator pause.
